_comment: Hindu expansion 175-drive J: Ramayana episodes B (Griffith 1870-74; Wilson VP for Sagara), public domain.

region.zh: 楞伽（象徵性定位，斯里蘭卡）

texts.period: Ramayana of Valmiki, oldest strata c. 2nd c. BCE-2nd c. CE (Griffith translation, 1870-74)

source.work: The Ramayan of Valmiki, trans. R. T. H. Griffith (1870-74), Sundara Kanda, burning of Lanka

summary.en: Caught and humiliated by Ravana's guards, Hanuman answered with his tail: soaked in oil, set alight, he leapt free and used it as a torch, burning palace after palace through Lanka's rooftops - sparing only the grove where Sita sat. The message delivered on the way out: next time it will not be a monkey with a burning tail.
summary.zh: 被羅波那衛隊擒獲羞辱後，哈奴曼以尾作答：浸油、點燃，他躍脫羅網，以其為火炬，沿楞伽屋頂逐宮焚燬——唯獨繞過悉多所在的林苑。臨別的訊息：下次來的不是一隻尾巴著火的猴子。

passages.text: The guards' insult was the plot's gift: they wrapped his tail in cloth and oil to burn him, and the monkey let them finish the torch before he moved. Shrunk, then sprung, he ran the city's ridgelines with a flame at his back: council halls, treasury, Ravana's own palace - the roofs went up one by one, and the sea-breeze carried the news. One grove he did not burn - the Ashoka grove where Sita waited; he doused his tail in the sea, took one last look at the enemy's capital, and leapt home over the ocean.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Ramayana, Sundara Kanda (Griffith 1870-74); not verbatim.

region.en: Lanka court and Rama's camp (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 楞伽王廷與羅摩營地（象徵性定位）

texts.period: Ramayana of Valmiki, oldest strata c. 2nd c. BCE-2nd c. CE (Griffith translation, 1870-74)

source.work: The Ramayan of Valmiki, trans. R. T. H. Griffith (1870-74), Yuddha Kanda, Vibhishana episode

summary.en: In Ravana's war council, the king's own brother Vibhishana said the unforgivable thing: give Sita back. Driven from the court with insults, he crossed the lines to Rama's camp - where the monkeys wanted to kill a rakshasa and Rama gave him shelter with one sentence: I take whoever comes to me, even once. The war's map changed hands that evening.
summary.zh: 在羅波那的戰爭廷議上，王的親弟維毗沙那說出不可饒恕之言：把悉多還回去。他被以侮辱逐出廷堂，越線投奔羅摩營地——猴族欲誅此羅剎，羅摩一句話收留他：凡來我此者，縱一次，我亦納之。戰爭的地圖於那個傍晚易手。

passages.text: The council's honest voice belonged to the king's brother: return the wife of another, or die with her stolen - and Ravana's answer drove the only counselor who loved him out of Lanka. At Rama's camp the rakshasa's arrival split the monkeys - a spy, said some - until Rama's rule was stated once: whoever comes to me for shelter, once, is mine to keep. Vibhishana's knowledge of the city's gates, the ocean's ford, Kumbhakarna's bed - the war was won with the enemy's brother as cartographer, and the epic's hardest question (is treason ever dharma?) answered with a shelter, not an argument.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Ramayana, Yuddha Kanda (Griffith 1870-74); not verbatim.

region.zh: 楞伽（象徵性定位，斯里蘭卡）

texts.period: Ramayana of Valmiki, oldest strata c. 2nd c. BCE-2nd c. CE (Griffith translation, 1870-74)

source.work: The Ramayan of Valmiki, trans. R. T. H. Griffith (1870-74), Yuddha Kanda, Kumbhakarna episode

summary.en: Ravana's giant brother slept six months at a stretch - the boon he had begged for eternity, mispronounced into eternal sleep. To wake him for the war, the rakshasas drove a thousand elephants over his body and hammered him with drums. He rose, ate his breakfast army, and asked the news; told that it was his brother's pride he was dying for, he went anyway - loyalty larger than judgment.
summary.zh: 羅波那的巨人弟弟一睡半年——本為求得永生而許之願，被誤唸成永眠。為喚其赴戰，羅剎們驅千象踩過其身，以鼓錘擊之。他起身，吞下早餐般的軍陣，問道新聞；得知自己是為兄長的驕傲而死，他仍然前往——忠誠大於判斷。

passages.text: The boon at Brahma's gate had been mispronounced: nirdeva-vamsha (lordship without gods) heard as nidra-vamsha (a race of sleep) - and the giant who asked for the world's end got an appointment book with half the year dark. To raise him for the war the rakshasas stampeded elephants across his chest and rang the city's drums against his ears; he rose yawning, asked what was for breakfast, and ate the first regiment sent to greet him.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Ramayana, Yuddha Kanda (Griffith 1870-74); not verbatim.

passages.text: Told the truth about the war - his brother's lust, not Lanka's honor - he chose his brother anyway: the epic's strangest loyalist, a giant who knew the cause was wrong and carried it to the field on his shoulders.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Ramayana, Yuddha Kanda (Griffith 1870-74); not verbatim.

title.zh: 因陀羅耆的蛇箭與蛇索

texts.period: Ramayana of Valmiki, oldest strata c. 2nd c. BCE-2nd c. CE (Griffith translation, 1870-74)

source.work: The Ramayan of Valmiki, trans. R. T. H. Griffith (1870-74), Yuddha Kanda, Indrajit's serpent weapons

summary.en: Ravana's son Indrajit, invisible in war-chariot and sorcery, twice came near to ending the war in an afternoon: once with the Naga-pasha, the serpent-noose that bound Rama and Lakshmana both, and once with the arrow that left Lakshmana dying. Both times the counter-spell was a bird's: Garuda's wings, at whose approach the serpents fled, and the Sanjivana herb borne by Hanuman.
summary.zh: 羅波那之子因陀羅耆，隱形於戰車與咒術之中，兩度幾乎在一個下午結束戰爭：一次以蛇索縛住羅摩與羅什曼那二人，一次以一箭令羅什曼那垂死。兩次的破解皆為飛禽：金翅鳥之翼——蛇族見之而逃——以及哈奴曼所攜的還魂藥草。

passages.text: Indrajit fought from the sky like a sound: invisible, his serpent-arrows became living nooses around the two brothers' bodies - and the sons of the Wind stood still, bound by snakes. The release came from above the food-chain: Garuda descended, and every serpent on the field let go - the bird that eats snakes had a claim on them older than any war. His second stroke - the Shakti that left Lakshmana dying - was answered by Hanuman's mountain: the whole peak of herbs flown north, the wound closed by the lift itself - the war's ambulance was a mountain.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Ramayana, Yuddha Kanda (Griffith 1870-74); not verbatim. / Paraphrase of Ramayana, Yuddha Kanda and Sundara Kanda (Griffith 1870-74); not verbatim.

region.en: Dronagiri / Sanjivani mountain (symbolic pin in the Himalaya)
region.zh: 德羅那吉里／還魂山（象徵性定位於喜馬拉雅）

texts.period: Ramayana of Valmiki, oldest strata c. 2nd c. BCE-2nd c. CE (Griffith translation, 1870-74)

source.work: The Ramayan of Valmiki, trans. R. T. H. Griffith (1870-74), Yuddha Kanda/Sundara Kanda, the Sanjivana mountain

summary.en: Lakshmana lay dying, and the physician-gods named the herb: Sanjivani, on a Himalayan peak that nobody could identify in time. Hanuman flew, failed to find the one plant among thousands, and solved it his way - he lifted the entire mountain and set it down on the battlefield. The mountain, the tradition says, has herbs still, and Himalayan villages argue about which peak it was.
summary.zh: 羅什曼那垂死，醫神指出藥草之名：還魂草，在喜馬拉雅一峰，無人能及時辨認。哈奴曼飛去，於千百藥草間無從分辨，遂以其法解之——舉起整座山，置於戰場之上。據傳統所說，那座山至今仍有藥草，喜馬拉雅村落至今仍爭論是哪一峰。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition (place-cults claim the peak); classified 'myth'.

passages.text: The diagnosis was divine: only the Sanjivani herb can bring him back, and it grows on a mountain of ten thousand look-alikes - the war had hours, not days. Hanuman flew north, searched the moonlit slope, and found the impossible shortlist: every plant in sight could be the one, and every minute cost blood.

His solution was scale itself: he uprooted the mountain, flew it south under one arm, and set it on the field - the herb wherever it was, delivered; and the peak he returned (whichever it truly was) has been argued over ever since.

title.en: Ravana's Last Stand and the Brahmastra
title.zh: 羅波那的最後一戰與婆羅摩箭

texts.period: Ramayana of Valmiki, oldest strata c. 2nd c. BCE-2nd c. CE (Griffith translation, 1870-74)

source.work: The Ramayan of Valmiki, trans. R. T. H. Griffith (1870-74), Yuddha Kanda, Ravana's death

summary.en: Ravana's last day had the shape of a first-rate king's: quivers emptied, crowns broken, heads regrown as they were struck off. The deaths that would not stay dead ended with a single arrow - the Brahmastra, aimed at the navel where the nectar of his immortality was stored. Ravana fell still defending his city, and Rama ordered the funeral rites of a hero for the enemy who had ruined him.
summary.zh: 羅波那的最後一日有第一流君王的形狀：箭囊傾空，王冠碎裂，被斬之首一次次重新長出。不會死去的死亡終於由一枝箭終結——婆羅摩箭，瞄準其不死甘露所藏之臍。羅波那仍在守衛其城時倒下，而羅摩為這位毀了他的敵人舉行英雄之葬。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition; Ravana's dignity is read differently across South Asia; classified 'myth'.

passages.text: The duel was regicide as repair-work: heads cut off grew back, crowns shattered and were replaced - a king being killed in installments because his death refused to complete. Vibhishana, from the enemy's side, named the secret: the nectar in the navel - and Rama's Brahmastra went where no blow had reached, and the ten heads came off to stay. The fallen king got a hero's pyre at his slayer's order: the scholar-king of Lanka, veena-player and city-builder, buried as an adversary should be - with the honors he had earned and the judgment he had refused.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Ramayana, Yuddha Kanda (Griffith 1870-74); not verbatim.

title.en: Lava and Kusha Sing the Epic in Their Father's Court
title.zh: 羅婆與俱舍於父廷誦唱史詩

region.zh: 蟻垤仙居與阿逾陀（象徵性定位）

texts.period: Ramayana of Valmiki, Uttara Kanda (critical edition appendix), c. 2nd c. BCE-2nd c. CE (Griffith translation, 1870-74)

source.work: The Ramayan of Valmiki, trans. R. T. H. Griffith (1870-74), Uttara Kanda, Lava and Kusha

summary.en: In Valmiki's forest school, two boys learned to sing a story they did not know was theirs: the exile, the abduction, the war - and the queen abandoned though proved pure. Brought to Ayodhya to sing before the court, they named their mother Sita and their father Rama, and the poem's audience discovered its own ending: the king had exiled a pregnant wife who was innocent by fire and by earth.
summary.zh: 在蟻垤的林中學堂，兩個男孩學唱一則不知屬於自己的故事：流放、被擄、戰爭——以及雖經證明清白仍被放棄的王后。他們被召至阿逾陀，於王廷獻唱，唱出其母悉多、其父羅摩之名，而詩的聽眾發現了自己的結局：這位王曾放逐一位以火與地雙證其清白的懷孕之妻。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition and contested narrative; classified 'myth'.

passages.text: The twins of the forest learned the poem as schoolwork: meter, melody, the whole career of a king who looked suspiciously like the founder of their song. Sung before the assembled court, the ballad came to its present - the queen proved by fire, and exiled pregnant all the same - and the hall went silent: the boys were singing the king's sin back to him.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Ramayana, Uttara Kanda (Griffith 1870-74); not verbatim.

passages.text: The family reunion is the poem's last test: Sita summoned to the assembly, calling the earth to witness once more - and the furrow opened and took its daughter; the epic ends by returning its heroine to the soil that made her.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Ramayana, Uttara Kanda (Griffith 1870-74); not verbatim.

title.en: The Pushpaka Chariot Flies Rama Home
title.zh: 布施帕迦飛車載羅摩歸國

region.zh: 自楞伽至阿逾陀（象徵性定位）

texts.period: Ramayana of Valmiki, oldest strata c. 2nd c. BCE-2nd c. CE (Griffith translation, 1870-74)

source.work: The Ramayan of Valmiki, trans. R. T. H. Griffith (1870-74), Yuddha Kanda, the Pushpaka chariot

summary.en: The flying palace-chariot of Kubera, taken by Ravana, fell to the victors: Rama ordered it to the Ashoka grove for Sita, and it carried her, the monkey army, and the story home - over the bridge, the forests, the hermitages of the exile, each stop telling its own part of the war. Ayodhya lit the city for a midnight arrival: the first Diwali, the tradition says.
summary.zh: 財神俱毘羅的飛行宮車曾為羅波那所奪，如今歸於勝者：羅摩令其飛往無憂林苑接悉多，載著她、猴軍與故事歸國——越過橋樑、森林、流亡的仙居，每一處停靠自述其在戰爭中的一節。阿逾陀燃城以待午夜歸人：傳統言，此即第一個排燈節。

passages.text: The chariot flew at its rider's thought: Sita seated in state, the monkey commanders in their fur, the sky-road taken south to north over a war's whole geography. Each stop was a rite of return: the bridge of stones, Rishyashringa's hermitage, Bharata's hut outside the capital - the exile's road traveled backward at flying speed. Ayodhya heard the drums and lit every lamp in the city for the midnight entry: fourteen years of darkness ending in a street of fire - the charter of the festival of lights.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Ramayana, Yuddha Kanda (Griffith 1870-74); not verbatim.

title.en: Kapila's Fire and the Sons of Sagara
title.zh: 迦毘羅之火與薩伽羅之子

region.en: Ocean depths (symbolic pin at Sagar Island)
region.zh: 海洋深處（象徵性定位於薩伽羅島）

texts.period: Vishnu Purana, Book IV (dynasty of Sagara), c. 300-800 CE (Wilson translation, 1840)

source.work: The Vishnu Purana, trans. H. H. Wilson (1840), Book IV, the sons of Sagara and Kapila's fire

summary.en: King Sagara's sixty thousand sons dug the ocean in search of a stolen horse and burned everything in their way. The sage Kapila, interrupted in meditation by the horde, opened his eyes and burned all sixty thousand to ash - souls imprisoned in unburnt bones that no water could wash. Many generations later, Bhagiratha's descent of the Ganga (over Shiva's hair) freed them: the ocean is called Sagara for the diggers.
summary.zh: 王薩伽羅的六萬子為尋被竊之馬掘穿大洋，沿途焚燬一切。仙人迦毘羅於禪定中被打擾，睜眼之間，六萬人皆化為灰——其靈魂囚於水洗不去的未化之骨。數代之後，跋吉羅陀引恆河下降（經濕婆之髮）而釋之：大洋至今以掘者之名為名（薩伽羅）。

passages.text: The sacrificial horse was stolen to the underworld sea; Sagara's sixty thousand sons dug after it, turning the earth into the great basin of the ocean in their search. The sage Kapila sat in the depths where their spades arrived; the army's clamor broke his meditation, and one opened eye was a furnace - sixty thousand sons of a king burned to a single ash-heap. The ashes were the debt: no rite could free the souls until the Ganga herself came down to touch them - and the sea the diggers made still carries their king's name.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Vishnu Purana, Book IV (Wilson 1840); not verbatim.

title.en: Rama and Shambuka: The Ascetic Death
title.zh: 羅摩與首薄迦：苦行者的死亡

region.zh: 阿逾陀城郊（象徵性定位）

texts.period: Ramayana of Valmiki, Uttara Kanda (critical edition appendix), c. 2nd c. BCE-2nd c. CE (Griffith translation, 1870-74)

source.work: The Ramayan of Valmiki, trans. R. T. H. Griffith (1870-74), Uttara Kanda, Shambuka episode

summary.en: A child of Ayodhya died young; the seers traced the cause to a disorder in the order of castes: a Shudra named Shambuka was practicing austerities reserved for the twice-born, upside-down on a tree-branch. Rama went, confirmed the tale, and struck off the ascetic's head - and the child revived. The episode is the epic's hardest scene: dharma as hierarchy enforced by the ideal king, and the modern argument about it has never closed.
summary.zh: 阿逾陀之一孩童夭折；仙人們究其因於種姓秩序之亂：一名首陀羅名首薄迦者，倒懸於樹枝之上，修習唯再生者可修之苦行。羅摩前往，證實其事，斬下苦行者之頭——孩童於是復活。此幕是史詩最沉重的一幕：正法被理想之王以等級執行；而圍繞它的現代論爭從未閉合。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition and politically contested (caste politics); classified 'myth'. The contested modern readings are recorded here.

passages.text: The diagnosis of the kingdom's grief came from the seers: an ascetic of the wrong caste was heating the world with penance, and a child of the city paid the price. Rama found Shambuka hanging head-down on the branch, emaciated and luminous, and asked him his name and his vow; the answer confirmed the seers' account. The sword fell - and the dead child sat up in Ayodhya as the ascetic's life went out: the episode has made the Uttara Kanda the most argued section of the epic, and modern retellings often refuse it outright.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Ramayana, Uttara Kanda (Griffith 1870-74); not verbatim.
